subject: Asteria7B staging pin exception and rollout agenda
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sylvia Park <sylvia@datasynth.ai>
Cc: Datasynth Procurement <procurement@datasynth.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0000
Subject: Request: temporary pin for Asteria7B (staging) + routing guardrails

Hi team — looping everyone for visibility.

Quick context: Datasynth (Sylvia) is ready to move an internal workload to Redwood next week but they've asked specifically for Asteria7B (7B) model variant; the vendor sent a build tagged v2.1-q8 which has slightly different tokenizer behavior and a changed kv-cache layout. Early integration tests (attached) show tokenization edge-cases for some multi-lingual prompts and slightly higher memory use on peak sequence lengths.

Ask: Can we agree to a short-lived staging pin to Asteria7B v2.1-q8 for the Datasynth workspace so they can validate in their environment, with the following protections:
- Temporarily pin model at staging for Datasynth only (no production global pin)
- Canary traffic: start at 1% for 48 hours then 10% for 24 hours
- Telemetry gating: fail open to v2.0 if tokenization errors spike >0.5% or latency P95 increases >200ms versus baseline
- Run tokenizer-adapter (attached patch) in the ingest path while infra lands a platform-side adapter

Attachments: asteria7b-compat-matrix.csv (summary tests), tokenizer-adapter-diff.patch, canary-playbook.md

Sylvia — can you confirm Datasynth's desired staging window (they proposed 2026-02-16 to 2026-02-18) and whether they can take the initial 1% canary traffic?

Laura / Karthik / Dev / Marissa — I'm asking for a one-time pin exception approval (48–72h) plus routing fallback policy. If we can get sign-off today, I can communicate the plan and lock the staging window with Datasynth.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sylvia Park <sylvia@datasynth.ai>, Datasynth Procurement <procurement@datasynth.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: temporary pin for Asteria7B (staging) + routing guardrails

Thanks Sean — high level looks fine, appreciate the attachments. A couple of product clarifications before I sign off:

1) Scope: Confirm this pin is limited to the Datasynth workspace and staging environment only (no shared routing or tenant bleed).
2) Rollback criteria: In addition to Telemetry gating thresholds, let's add a content-regression check against the canonical prompt set (we should see no >1.5% drop in Rouge-L / exact-match on the sample prompts).
3) Timeline: 48–72h staging pin is OK but prefer we keep it to 48h unless Datasynth explicitly needs longer.

Action for me: I'll prepare a short PRD addendum and the canonical prompt set to run during the canary (will send the doc link shortly). Dev / Karthik — can you confirm implementation feasibility for per-tenant pinning and routing fallback to v2.0?

Laura Bennett
Senior Product Manager, Model Safety & Ops | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 13:37:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: temporary pin for Asteria7B (staging) + routing guardrails

Thanks — short answers:
- Per-tenant staging pin: feasible. We'll implement a workspace-scoped routing rule that prefers Asteria7B v2.1-q8 for Datasynth's staging tag. No ripple to other tenants.
- Fallback routing: implement route-by-policy: if telemetry probe fails (tokenizer error rate or P95 latency), traffic will be rebalanced to Asteria7B v2.0 automatically. That will be handled by the routing controller; expected work: ~8 engineer-hours of config + 2h for smoke tests.
- Memory/cost: the v2.1-q8 variant uses ~12% more peak GPU RAM for long sequences; for staging at 1% traffic we should be fine but we need to reserve a buffer for burst.

I'll create a routing branch and a short runbook for the ops crew. I'll also vet the tokenizer-adapter-diff.patch and run the unit tests later today.

Dev Patel
Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 09:20:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: temporary pin for Asteria7B (staging) + routing guardrails

+1 to the plan with one operational constraint: we need a signed mutual action plan from Datasynth confirming test windows and rollback acceptance before we apply the pin. We should also gate the pin behind a lightweight canary verification job that runs the canonical prompt set Laura mentioned and the quick KV-cache-consistency check (I reviewed the compat CSV).

Proposed minimal checklist for approval (Karthik):
- Datasynth MPA (dates + rollback acceptance) signed
- Canary routing rule implemented by infra (Dev) and smoke-tested in staging cluster
- Telemetry thresholds wired into the circuit-breaker (Dev + Marissa)
- Product confirmation on canonical prompt set (Laura)

If those four items are green I'm OK to approve a 48h staging pin. After 48h we either drop the pin or extend by exception with explicit exec sign-off.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Release Engineering | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
